I have been farming this land in Quzhou for more than fifty years. My boys left for the city long ago, so I manage mostly by myself now, though I hire a machine team for the heavy work. I cannot do things the way I used to at 40, but I know this land well.

Every year it is the same rotation — winter wheat, then summer maize on the same fields. Everyone here does it, and it has always fed my family. I am not going to try something new at my age. I have about 8 mu of land I work.

For the wheat — I planted it last October as I always do. I will give it another irrigation now that spring is here, one more at jointing, and one at grain fill. I apply compound fertilizer as base and urea as topdressing at jointing, about the same amounts I have used for twenty years. The county extension office once told me to use less nitrogen, but I worry about low yield, so I keep my own amounts. I will spray once for weeds and once for aphids and powdery mildew.

For the maize — I will plant it right after the wheat harvest in June, using the hybrid seed from the township supply co-op. Everyone uses 郑单958 type. I will have the machine team direct-seed it without plowing again since the soil is already loose. Summer rain usually covers most water needs but I will irrigate twice if it is dry. I spray herbicide right after planting and check for corn borer in mid-season.

I am 73 and my knees are not good. I hire out the combine harvesting and the rotary tilling. That is the main outside cost.
